correctness.rationale: The exact 14-dimensional binary vanishing space is independently constructed by row reduction. For all 139 projective equation orbits, affine-chart Jacobian Groebner ideals identify exactly 10 smooth orbits/1512 smooth forms. A separately implemented C++ finite-field gradient test over extension degrees 1 through 10 agrees. The genus-six normalization formula bounds the geometric singular Frobenius degree by 10 for reduced plane quintics; nonreduced quintics have a repeated factor of degree <=2 with an F2-rational zero. Thus both smoothness checks are mathematically exhaustive, not finite guesses. Exact XOR subspace enumeration gives 16800 pencils, and the 168-element projective-group action gives 108 orbits: 96 of length 168 and 12 of length 56. Each program independently recovers the same 672/3024/13104 member-type distribution and orbit–stabilizer orders. The 108 representative masks and their class types are regenerated and compared byte-for-byte with the packaged CSV. Basepoint transversality follows from three nonzero gradients in a two-dimensional F2 cotangent space, and Bezout yields residual length 18.

value.rationale: The subject is the entire moduli of basepoint-constrained smooth pencils at the first postminimal plane-filling degree q+3 over the smallest field, combining two motivating published directions. A complete classification of all such pencils, rather than an arbitrary numerical slice, is a natural extremal finite-field geometry question. The new 108 projective orbits and the dichotomy between trivial stabilizer and cyclic order-three symmetry, recognized exactly by whether their three members share one individual orbit type, give geometric structure not captured by single-curve totals. The base-scheme transversality and length-18 residual intersection place the count in the geometry of linear systems; no downstream theorem or broad-field generalization is asserted.
